sources.entry: Daily Stars Explorer ⚠ - Track GitHub repo trends with daily star insights to see growth and community interest over time. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Go/Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: A web tool that charts the full daily star history of any GitHub repository, alongside commits, PRs, issues, forks, contributors, and feed mentions.
summary.what_it_does: Daily Stars Explorer takes any GitHub repo and builds a daily star-count chart from GitHub's star history endpoint, which returns aggregated weekly buckets with daily breakdowns. It also shows activity timelines for commits, PRs, issues, forks, and contributors, which use the GraphQL API and require a personal access token. Feed mentions from HN, Reddit, YouTube, and GitHub can be overlaid on the star chart to show what was said when a spike happened. Users can compare two repos side by side, pin favorites, export data as CSV or JSON, and use dark mode. Fetched data is cached for 7 days, and later visits only pull new stars. The README also references an aggregate.md document describing moving averages, LOESS smoothing, and derivatives.
use_cases: Check whether a GitHub repo's star growth is steady or driven by a single spike
Compare the popularity trajectories of two libraries side by side
Find out which HN, Reddit, or YouTube posts coincided with a star spike
Export repo star and activity data to CSV or JSON for analysis
Review a project's commit, PR, and issue activity over time
Self-host a personal GitHub star-history dashboard via Docker
how_to_run: Local development: cp .env.example .env && go run main.go (backend)
cd website && npm install && npm start (frontend, separate terminal)
notable: Star history rebuilt from GitHub's 2026 aggregate endpoint, so a full history takes roughly 1 to 33 requests and about a second or two
Star charts work without a PAT, though commits, PRs, issues, forks, and contributors still need one
Overlays feed mentions from HN, Reddit, YouTube, and GitHub on the star curve to explain spikes
Hourly star resolution has been retired because GitHub no longer exposes per-stargazer timestamps
caveats: Hourly star charts are no longer available because GitHub removed per-stargazer timestamps
Commits, PRs, issues, forks, and contributor timelines still need a GitHub PAT and the GraphQL API
Star totals can differ from stargazers_count by a star or two due to deleted or suspended accounts
The README says error handling is limited and the UI and code quality could be improved
keywords: see when a repo went viral
